prompt: Company profile: Beverage bottling plant in Olathe, Kansas; 110 employees. Situation: After a fleet and equipment expansion, a year-end inventory shows: 14,000 pounds of propane on site for fleet fueling and heaters, and about 900 pounds of sulfuric acid contained in forklift and UPS batteries. Neither chemical previously exceeded any reporting threshold. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register — including any thresholds that are NOT crossed. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
This analysis identifies the compliance obligations arising from the inventory levels of Propane and Sulfuric Acid at the Olathe, Kansas facility. The primary regulatory framework governing these chemicals is the **Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA)**, enforced in Kansas by the **Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE)**.

Note: While the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations apply to the *use* of these chemicals, the specific "inventory level" triggers described in the situation primarily activate EPCRA reporting obligations.

### 1. EPCRA Section 312 – Tier II Chemical Reporting (State of Kansas)

*   **Requirement:** Annual submission of a Tier II Emergency and Hazardous Chemical Inventory Form to the State Emergency Response Commission (SERC), Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC), and local fire department.
*   **Source:** EPCRA Section 312; Kansas Statute 65-5701 et seq. (Kansas Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act).
*   **Applicability:** This obligation is **triggered** for both chemicals.
    *   **Thresholds Crossed:**
        *   **Propane:** The reporting threshold for "Extremely Hazardous Substances" (EHS) is 500 lbs (or the TPQ, whichever is lower). Propane is listed on the CERCLA list, but often treated under EHS or hazardous chemical categories depending on state-specific implementation. However, under standard EPCRA Section 312, for EHS chemicals, the threshold is 500 lbs. With 14,000 lbs on site, the threshold is significantly exceeded.
        *   **Sulfuric Acid:** Sulfuric Acid is an EHS. The Section 312 reporting threshold for an EHS is 500 lbs (or the TPQ). With 900 lbs on site, the company exceeds the 500 lb threshold.
    *   *Note on Thresholds NOT Crossed:* The **Section 311** (SDS reporting) threshold is typically 10,000 lbs for non-EHS hazardous chemicals. While Propane exceeds this, Sulfuric Acid (900 lbs) does not exceed the 10,000 lb threshold *if it were not an EHS*. However, because Sulfuric Acid is an EHS, its threshold drops to 500 lbs, triggering the reporting requirement where a non-EHS would have been exempt.
*   **ISO Clause:** ISO 14001 6.1.3 (Determining compliance obligations); ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Determining compliance obligations).
*   **Evaluation (9.1.2):**
    *   **How:** The Environmental Manager must verify the maximum amount of each chemical stored on-site during the calendar year against the Kansas Tier II reporting thresholds. They must submit the electronic report via the Kansas Tier II Reporting System (K-TIER II).
    *   **When:** Annually. The inventory is taken as of December 31st (Year-End), and the report must be submitted by **March 1st** of the following year.

### 2. EPCRA Section 302 – Emergency Planning Notification

*   **Requirement:** Notification to the SERC and LEPC that the facility is subject to emergency planning requirements because it holds an Extremely Hazardous Substance (EHS) above the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ).
*   **Source:** EPCRA Section 302; 40 CFR 355.
*   **Applicability:** **Not Applicable (Threshold NOT Crossed).**
    *   **Threshold Analysis:** Sulfuric Acid is an EHS with a Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ) of **1,000 lbs** (based on the standard listing for sulfuric acid, though concentration matters, pure acid is usually 1,000 lbs).
    *   **Status:** The site has 900 lbs of sulfuric acid. Because 900 lbs < 1,000 lbs, the facility is **not** required to notify the SERC/LEPC under Section 302 for emergency planning purposes.
    *   **Propane Note:** Propane is generally not listed as an EHS under Section 302, so it does not trigger this specific obligation.
*   **ISO Clause:** ISO 14001 6.1.3.
*   **Evaluation (9.1.2):**
    *   **How:** Review the annual inventory against the Section 302 TPQ list (40 CFR 355, Appendix A). Document the negative finding (i.e., "900 lbs stored vs. 1,000 lb TPQ; Section 302 not triggered").
    *   **When:** Annually, during the year-end inventory review process.

### 3. OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) & Process Safety Management (PSM)

*   **Requirement:** Maintain Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all hazardous chemicals and ensure proper labeling. Additionally, evaluate if Process Safety Management (PSM) applies to the propane.
*   **Source:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 (HCS); 29 CFR 1910.119 (PSM).
*   **Applicability:**
    *   **HCS:** Applicable. The company must have SDSs accessible for both Propane and Sulfuric Acid (batteries).
    *   **PSM (Threshold Analysis):** PSM applies to flammable gases (Propane) if the quantity exceeds **10,000 lbs**.
    *   **Status:** The site has 14,000 lbs of propane.
    *   **Result:** The **10,000 lb threshold IS crossed**. This creates a significant obligation to develop a Process Safety Management program for the propane storage/fueling area (including process safety information, operating procedures, training, management of change, etc.).
*   **ISO Clause:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Legal requirements regarding OH&S hazards).
*   **Evaluation (9.1.2):**
    *   **How:** Conduct a compliance audit to verify PSM program elements are in place (process hazard analysis, mechanical integrity, etc.).
    *   **When:** PSM compliance must be maintained continuously. A formal compliance audit is required at least every three years (per OSHA PSM requirements), but internal checks should occur annually.

### 4. Kansas Storage Tank Regulations

*   **Requirement:** Registration and regulation of aboveground storage tanks (ASTs).
*   **Source:** Kansas Storage Tank Act (K.S.A. 65-6401 et seq.).
*   **Applicability:** **Triggered.**
    *   **Threshold Analysis:** Kansas requires registration for ASTs storing regulated substances (like propane) with a capacity greater than 660 gallons (approx. 2,500 lbs of propane) or aggregate capacity greater than 1,320 gallons.
    *   **Status:** With 14,000 lbs on site, the fleet fueling system likely consists of one or more tanks exceeding these capacities.
    *   **Obligation:** The facility must ensure the tanks are registered with KDHE and comply with spill prevention/secondary containment requirements (though secondary containment for propane gas is physically different than liquid fuels).
*   **ISO Clause:** ISO 14001 6.1.3.
*   **Evaluation (9.1.2):**
    *   **How:** Verify current registration certificates are posted and tanks have been inspected by a certified inspector as required by Kansas law.
    *   **When:** Annual renewal of registration; periodic tank inspections per state schedule.

### Summary of Compliance Obligations Register Update

| Obligation | Requirement Source | Threshold Status | Action Required | ISO Clause | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier II Reporting** | EPCRA 312 / Kansas Statute | **CROSSED** (Propane >500lbs; Sulfuric Acid >500lbs) | Submit Tier II report to SERC/LEPC/Fire Dept by March 1. | 14001 6.1.3 | Annual submission (March 1). |
| **Emergency Planning (Sec 302)** | EPCRA 302 | **NOT CROSSED** (Sulfuric Acid < 1,000 lbs TPQ) | No action required. Document exemption. | 14001 6.1.3 | Annual inventory review. |
| **Process Safety Management** | OSHA 1910.119 | **CROSSED** (Propane > 10,000 lbs) | Implement full PSM program for propane area. | 45001 6.1.3 | Continuous maintenance; 3-year audit cycle. |
| **Hazard Communication** | OSHA 1910.1200 | N/A (Applies to use) | Maintain SDSs and labels. | 45001 6.1.3 | Annual review of SDS library. |
